questions.q: What happens if you ask an LLM 'which table has customer churn data?' without any grounding?
options: It either says it doesn't know, or guesses a plausible-sounding table name that doesn't actually exist in your workspace
It always returns the exact correct table name with full certainty
It automatically connects to your Fabric workspace to check
It refuses to answer any question about tables
questions.explain: The model's knowledge comes from training data with a cutoff — it has never seen your specific workspace's metadata.

questions.q: What does 'grounding' mean in the context of RAG?
options: Giving the model actual, current, relevant content at question time instead of relying on what it memorized during training
Training a brand-new model from scratch on your data
Disabling the model's ability to generate any text
Asking the model to guess more confidently
questions.explain: RAG is the standard pattern for grounding an LLM's answer in real, current, relevant information rather than training-data memory.

questions.q: What are the four stages of the RAG pipeline, in order?
options: Embed, index, retrieve, generate
Generate, retrieve, index, embed
Train, test, validate, deploy
Extract, transform, load, report
questions.explain: Content is embedded into vectors, those vectors are indexed for fast search, relevant ones are retrieved at question time, and the LLM generates an answer from them.

questions.q: Why does the embedding stage matter for retrieval quality?
options: It makes text comparable by meaning rather than exact keyword matching, so related terms like 'customer churn' and 'customer attrition' land close together
It deletes the original text so only vectors remain
It has no effect on search quality at all
It only works for numeric data, never for text
questions.explain: Embeddings capture meaning as vectors, which is what allows similarity search to find conceptually related content even without shared keywords.

questions.q: Why does this lesson stay conceptual rather than building an actual index?
options: Because Lesson 51 covers chunking and actually building a vector index, and Lesson 52 wires the full retrieve-and-generate loop into a working example
Because building a vector index is impossible in Microsoft Fabric
Because RAG has no practical implementation anywhere in this course
Because embeddings are purely theoretical and never used in practice
questions.explain: This lesson establishes the pipeline shape; the next two lessons make it concrete, building up to a RAG pipeline over Fabric's own metadata catalog.
